text:
emily: Quick sync — ACME asks for sealed bundles + zero-touch updates for their air-gapped POC. They want: signed bundles, SBOM/provenance, offline activation, and a clear upgrade cadence. @raj can you weigh in on feasibility?

raj: Feasible. We support HSM-backed signing (PKCS#11) and detached signatures for tarballs. Verification is simple on their side: import vendor public cert, run signature verify. For delta updates we prefer signed delta bundles to keep size small.

sam: Recommend cadence: quarterly full bundle + monthly delta patches. Emergency patches outside cadence possible but need a signed emergency patch process. Rollback is label-based (keep last N bundles). Concern: delta chunking needs manifest to ensure idempotent apply.

maria: Clarify: their "zero-touch" requirement means ops should not run manual unpack+verify. They want an automated install-agent that validates signature and applies during a maintenance window. Also asked if activation can be offline (no phone-home).

customer-sre: Correct — no phone-home. We can accept offline activation tokens or pre-signed license blobs bound to customer HW fingerprint. They will only import vendor_pub.pem and a license blob. Also require proof-of-origin (SBOM).

raj: Suggested end-to-end flow:
1) CI builds bundle -> produce bundle.tar.gz + bundle.sig (signed with vendor HSM) + sbom.json + manifest.json
2) Upload artifact to customer drop (scp/usb)
3) Customer installer verifies signature against vendor_pub.pem, validates SBOM, verifies manifest, applies delta or full bundle
Offline activation: customer generates a nonce and gives to vendor (via signed channel), vendor returns a signed JWT-like activation token. Verification uses vendor_pub.

Example verification snippet we can include in runbook:
```
# verify and extract bundle
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify vendor_pub.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
tar -xzf bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood
```

Also: key rotation — vendor rotates signing key annually, publishes new vendor_pub via signed manifest. Customer should allow multiple active pub keys for a short overlap window.

deploy-bot: Artifact uploaded to ACME dropbox: sha256=abcd1234ef567890..., bundle.sig present, sbom.json present :package:

emily: Two commercial/legal asks before we lock SOW: 1) SBOM & provenance commitment 2) SLA for emergency patches (business days). Legal wants explicit wording for patch timelines.

legal: We need the engineering commit in writing. Wording proposal: "Redwood will provide emergency signed patches for Severity 1 defects within 7 business days of confirmed reproduction." Does engineering agree?

maria: Engineering can commit to 7 business days for Sev1 emergency patches. Non-sev1 monthly delta cadence. Will surface to support for inclusion in SOW. :white_check_mark:

customer-sre: Also request a one-page runbook with commands for verification, rollback steps, and key rotation steps. If we get that + a sample signed activation token flow by Friday we can schedule PO delivery week of next month.

raj: I'll draft the runbook + verification snippets and sample manifests. Target: EOD Thursday.

sam: I'll confirm max delta bundle size and the agent behaviour for zero-touch installs (timeouts, retry/backoff) and send specifics to the runbook.

emily: Action items recap: raj -> runbook + sample tokens (EOD Thu); sam -> delta limits + agent behaviour; maria -> confirm SLA text for SOW; legal -> ready to review wording. I'll loop in ACME procurement once runbook is ready. :memo: :rocket:

customer-sre: Thanks — looking forward to the runbook. If possible include sample key rotation commands and how to revoke a vendor_pub in their offline verifier.

raj: Will include revoke/rotate procedures and an emergency rollback checklist.

emily: Great. If there are any blockers (HSM integration complexity, licensing binding to HW fingerprint) call them out in the runbook so procurement can decide.

customer-sre: Appreciated. Ping me when docs are uploaded.
